question: Can a failed native principal refund itself fail, leaving zero merchant delivery and zero successful principal recovery despite FINAL completion?
source: nearcore bc4e9e8cfb03d9e82f027883055624e18576993e runtime/runtime/src/lib.rs system-refund failure branch lines1047–1056
fixture: Official deliberately unrestricted rs_contract WASM in isolated local sandbox2.14.0/protocol88; no business guard or live model

cases.expected: Original transfer fails; one successful system principal refund returns1 NEAR to vault.

cases.refund_to: A second explicitly absent named account
cases.expected: Original transfer fails; system principal refund also fails; no successful principal refund or merchant payout. Source predicts refund burn rather than another automatic refund.

controls: Verify both account absences with explicit UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT; capture all raw local RPC outcomes, parent-child references, amount and refund signer markers. Record before/after balances and block total_supply as supporting observations; do not equate account delta to exact principal because gas rewards may contribute.
interpretation_limits: Native no-delivery alone does not establish principal recovered or zero loss.
A burn attribution combines observed failed system refund with pinned runtime semantics; do not call it a protocol vulnerability.
No external network, payments, wallets, model or submitted contest action.
Record failure rather than change protocol/settings to force expected result.
